statements.text: And when you think about the overall overarching subjects that the Energy and Commerce Committee deals with, which is a lot of different topics outside of the subcommittee, one of the issues that we talk about is the dangers of the environment and climate change. [...] when you throw Section 230 and you mix it with what we are seeing with AI, I think that AI may kill all of us before climate change will if we don't do something about everything that is happening in this particular space.
statements.context: House Energy and Commerce subcommittee hearing on proposals to sunset or reform Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act.

statements.text: Okay. So given that the Air Force's focus on is on developing these AI-piloted jets, how could a V-BAT—because I know the F-35 has come up—how can V-BAT teams be complementary to F-35s? And how can Shield AI's technology enhance the effectiveness of the F-35 in joint operations?
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on Department of Defense acquisition, questioning a defense industry witness about AI-piloted drone platforms.

statements.text: However, we also have to acknowledge that there are some risks involved with AI that we need to continue to be talking about, that we are not mentioning enough. [...] And, unfortunately, one of the things I am worried about is President Trump's recent Executive order, titled, ``Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence,'' because I think that has undermined some essential AI protections that are accelerating the unchecked spread of AI across the country. And so I wanted to ask Dr. Reynolds, what measures do you think Congress should take to mitigate the increased risk of cyber attacks and other threats to our national security as manufacturing increasingly adopts to AI without sufficient regulation?
statements.context: House committee hearing on AI in manufacturing, where Rep. Veasey questions a witness about AI risks and regulatory needs.

statements.text: And with a massive growth of data centers and AI infrastructure that is happening right now, it is putting a tremendous strain on the grid.
statements.context: House Energy and Commerce Committee member questions a witness at a hearing on AI infrastructure and energy demand.

statements.text: I wanted to ask Ms. Kak: If this 10-year moratorium on State laws goes into effect, it is important to establish that we have clear Federal regulations to govern the use of AI in law enforcement. Do you agree with that?
statements.context: Congressional hearing titled 'AI Regulation and the Future of U.S. Leadership,' where Rep. Veasey questions a witness about facial recognition in policing and federal AI oversight.

statements.text: What can we do in order to make sure that there is consumer confidence in these areas of facial recognition and AI technology as we move forward to make sure that civil liberties are being met but to also make sure that anything that is being deployed, that the U.S. is the leader on that?
statements.context: Remarks during a hearing titled 'AI Regulation and the Future of U.S. Leadership,' held in the House Energy and Commerce Committee's Subcommittee on Communications and Technology.

statements.text: Yes, so how could this—back to you, Mrs. Chase. How could this regulatory tension influence the United States' position in the global race for leadership in AI against our competitors in China?
statements.context: Question posed by Rep. Veasey during a House hearing on NHTSA and motor vehicle safety.

statements.text: I know that a faulty language model may be annoying, but a faulty AI in an autonomous car can kill or injure, and the stakes are very high.
statements.context: House Energy and Commerce oversight hearing on NHTSA and motor vehicle safety, featuring a question to a witness about AV regulation.

statements.text: And one of the reasons why is because we really are relying on the 20th century power structure to help us figure out how we are going to through the 21st century AI manufacturing revolution.
statements.context: Verbatim remarks by Rep. Veasey during a congressional hearing on AI-driven electricity demand and grid modernization.
